title: India's Q1 Earnings Deliver Strong Beats: UltraTech Cement Profit Up 17%, Sobha Triples
excerpt: A wave of Q1 FY27 results shows broad-based strength across construction, real estate, and power sectors, even as oil-driven market volatility clouds the outlook.
body:
• UltraTech Cement posted a 17% rise in consolidated net profit to ₹2,599 crore for Q1 FY27, driven by higher volumes and improved pricing.
  • Sobha's profit more than tripled to ₹51 crore on revenue of ₹1,330 crore, reflecting a recovery in India's real estate sector.
  • Jaiprakash Power posted a 69% profit jump; Mahindra Logistics saw profit rise nearly fivefold to ₹29 crore.
  • Results come amid broader market anxiety over surging oil prices and rupee weakness from the US-Iran conflict.

India's Q1 FY27 earnings season gathered momentum on Monday with a string of strong results across cement, real estate, and infrastructure sectors, offering investors a counterpoint to the macroeconomic anxiety gripping markets over oil prices and the weakening rupee.

UltraTech Cement: Record Quarter

India's largest cement maker, UltraTech Cement, reported a 17% year-on-year rise in consolidated net profit to ₹2,599 crore for the June quarter. Revenue climbed 16% to ₹24,648 crore, while EBITDA rose 12% to ₹5,146 crore, supported by higher cement volumes and improved sales realisation of ₹5,218 per tonne.

The Aditya Birla Group flagship crossed a significant milestone during the quarter, surpassing 200 MTPA in domestic grey cement capacity and 205 MTPA globally. The company also commissioned 20 MW of waste heat recovery capacity and advanced its ₹1,800 crore entry into wires and cables, with the first plant expected to launch by year-end.

The India Cements subsidiary, acquired in late 2024, continued its turnaround under UltraTech's management, further consolidating the company's market leadership.

Sobha and the Real Estate Surge

Realty firm Sobha delivered a standout quarter, reporting a more than threefold increase in consolidated net profit to ₹50.84 crore, up from ₹13.61 crore a year ago. Total income rose to ₹1,330 crore from ₹901 crore, reflecting sustained demand in India's housing market.

The results align with a broader resurgence in Indian real estate, driven by urban migration, rising incomes, and a still-low mortgage rate environment. For NRI investors, who have been active buyers in Indian property markets, the strong fundamentals offer continued confidence.

Power and Logistics Also Shine

Jaiprakash Power Ventures posted a nearly 69% jump in consolidated net profit to ₹469 crore, buoyed by higher revenues. Mahindra Logistics saw profit surge nearly fivefold to ₹29 crore, with revenue jumping 23% to ₹1,655 crore as India's consumption-driven economy fueled demand for supply chain services.

What Investors Should Watch

The strong results come during what promises to be India's biggest earnings week of the quarter. Paytm, which saw a cross-candidate duplicate flagged in the selection process, Bluestone, and several other firms are set to report this week. But the macro picture is complicated — surging oil prices, rupee weakness, and the RBI's expected rate response could weigh on forward guidance.

For diaspora investors with India exposure, the earnings season offers a nuanced signal: corporate fundamentals remain robust, but the geopolitical premium on energy costs demands careful portfolio positioning.
